_note: SF neighborhood content, districts 1-4. Prose is grounded in geography, housing stock and transit — things checkable from a map. No founding dates, developer names or specific addresses beyond well-known landmarks. District rosters are inferred and need MLS verification.

neighborhoods.name: Sea Cliff
neighborhoods.intro: Sea Cliff sits on the bluffs above China Beach at the city's northwest corner, a small enclave of large detached houses on unusually generous lots. Its streets end at the Pacific, and the Golden Gate views from the northern blocks set the ceiling for the whole district.
near: Two sheltered coves at the foot of the neighborhood
Coastal trail and cypress groves along the headland
The Richmond's main retail corridor, a short drive east

neighborhoods.name: Lake Street
neighborhoods.intro: Lake Street runs along the Presidio's southern wall, a quiet corridor of wide lots and substantial pre-war homes. It is one of the calmest addresses in the Richmond, with the park immediately to the north and Clement Street's shops a few blocks south.
near: 1,500 acres of national parkland directly north
One of the district's public middle schools

neighborhoods.name: Inner Richmond
neighborhoods.intro: The Inner Richmond is the district's most walkable end, sitting between Golden Gate Park and the Presidio with Clement Street running through its center. Edwardian flats and small apartment buildings dominate, with detached houses appearing on the quieter northern blocks.
near: One of the city's great food streets, dense and independent
The park's northeast corner is a block away

neighborhoods.name: Central Richmond
neighborhoods.intro: Central Richmond is the flat, family-scaled middle of the district — a regular grid of Edwardian and marina-style homes on 25-foot lots, most with garages below. It trades convenience for calm, sitting between the Inner Richmond's retail and the ocean.
near: The park runs the full southern boundary
Rapid bus service the length of the district

neighborhoods.name: Outer Richmond
neighborhoods.intro: The Outer Richmond runs west toward Ocean Beach, foggier and more affordable than the blocks inland. The housing is consistent — rows of two-story homes over garages — and the Pacific is walkable from most of it.
near: Four miles of Pacific frontage at the western edge
Coastal trails at the northwest corner

neighborhoods.name: Jordan Park & Laurel Heights
neighborhoods.intro: Jordan Park and Laurel Heights form a small, established pocket just east of Arguello, with larger homes on quieter streets than the Richmond grid to the west. It sits high enough to catch light the avenues often miss.
near: A compact retail row on California Street

neighborhoods.name: Lone Mountain
neighborhoods.intro: Lone Mountain climbs the hill around the University of San Francisco at the district's southeast corner. The stock is a mix of Edwardian flats and detached homes, and the elevation gives many of the upper blocks long views east.
near: The campus sits at the center of the neighborhood
The Panhandle is a short walk south
Everyday retail at the foot of the hill

neighborhoods.name: Lincoln Park
neighborhoods.intro: Lincoln Park is parkland at the city's northwest tip, wrapping the Legion of Honor and the coastal trail at Lands End. It appears in the neighborhood map as a boundary rather than a residential area.
near: Golf course, coastal trail and cypress groves
The fine arts museum on the bluff
A sheltered cove below the headland

neighborhoods.name: Inner Sunset
neighborhoods.intro: The Inner Sunset is the district's most connected end, sitting where Golden Gate Park meets UCSF's Parnassus campus. Irving Street carries the retail, and the N-Judah runs straight downtown from the neighborhood's center.
near: The district's densest retail and restaurant strip
Directly north, with the botanical garden at the edge
Muni Metro downtown from Irving and 9th

neighborhoods.name: Central Sunset
neighborhoods.intro: Central Sunset is the archetype of the district — a regular grid of 1930s and 1940s tunnel-entrance houses, garages below, level entries, remarkably consistent block to block. It is one of the busiest single-family markets in San Francisco by volume.
near: Two Muni Metro lines serve the district
The park forms the northern boundary

neighborhoods.name: Outer Sunset
neighborhoods.intro: The Outer Sunset runs to the ocean, foggier than the blocks inland and long the most attainable end of the district. The stock matches the rest of the Sunset grid, and the beach is walkable from most of it.
near: The Pacific at the western edge, with the Great Highway beyond
Neighborhood corridors that have drawn newer cafes and shops
Muni Metro to downtown along Judah

neighborhoods.name: Inner Parkside
neighborhoods.intro: Inner Parkside sits between Taraval and the hill, close enough to West Portal to use its shops and station. The housing follows the Sunset pattern, with some larger lots against the slope.
near: A village-scaled main street just east
Eucalyptus canyon and summer concerts nearby

neighborhoods.name: Parkside
neighborhoods.intro: Parkside lies south of Taraval on the same consistent grid, quiet and steadily built. It is a high-volume market with stock that varies little from block to block.
near: A eucalyptus canyon with a summer concert series
Muni Metro running the length of Taraval

neighborhoods.name: Outer Parkside
neighborhoods.intro: Outer Parkside occupies the district's southwest corner, near the zoo and the southern end of Ocean Beach. It is among the most affordable single-family ground in the Sunset.
near: The Pacific at the western edge

neighborhoods.name: Golden Gate Heights
neighborhoods.intro: Golden Gate Heights rises above the Sunset grid on the hill's western slope, and the elevation is the point — many blocks carry long ocean views the flats do not. It is the district's premium pocket, with more varied architecture than the avenues below.
near: Hillside open space within the neighborhood
Muni Metro at the foot of the hill

neighborhoods.name: Pinelake Park
neighborhoods.intro: Pinelake Park is a small pocket beside Stern Grove at the district's southern edge, backing onto the lake and the eucalyptus canyon. It is quiet and largely detached, with the grove serving as its back garden.
near: Canyon parkland and a freshwater lake
Everyday retail along the southern edge
Muni Metro a short walk north

neighborhoods.name: Golden Gate Park
neighborhoods.intro: Golden Gate Park runs three miles from the Haight to the ocean and forms the northern boundary of this district. It appears in the neighborhood map as parkland rather than a residential area.
near: 1,017 acres of gardens, lakes and meadows
Two major museums in the park's center
The park's western end meets the Pacific

neighborhoods.name: Lakeside
neighborhoods.intro: Lakeside sits on curving streets near Lake Merced, with established homes on lots larger than most of the city's west side. It is quiet, well-treed and close to both the lake and Stonestown.
near: A freshwater lake with a four-mile loop
The city's major west-side shopping center

neighborhoods.name: Lakeshore
neighborhoods.intro: Lakeshore occupies the ground between Lake Merced and the ocean at the city's southwest corner. It is a mix of detached homes and larger residential complexes, with parkland on two sides.
near: The lake and its loop trail immediately east
Coastal bluffs and trails to the west

neighborhoods.name: Merced Manor
neighborhoods.intro: Merced Manor is a compact pocket of consistent 1930s stock between Sloat and the lake. It is small enough that few homes trade in any given quarter.
near: Everyday retail along the northern edge

neighborhoods.name: Merced Heights
neighborhoods.intro: Merced Heights sits on elevated ground at the district's southern end, with views south toward Daly City. The stock is modest and largely detached, on a regular grid.
near: A small hilltop park with wide views
The campus is a short distance northwest

neighborhoods.name: Ingleside
neighborhoods.intro: Ingleside is the district's largest neighborhood and one of the more attainable single-family markets in San Francisco. The housing is a mix of 1920s bungalows and post-war stock on a flat grid.
near: BART and Muni Metro at the eastern edge

neighborhoods.name: Ingleside Heights
neighborhoods.intro: Ingleside Heights climbs the southern slope toward the Daly City line, with modest homes on curving streets. It is among the most affordable ground in the city.
near: Hilltop open space with southern views

neighborhoods.name: Oceanview
neighborhoods.intro: Oceanview occupies a flat grid at the district's southeast, with modest detached homes and some of the lowest prices in San Francisco. Broad Street and Randolph carry its everyday retail.
near: A small park on the ridge above
BART and Muni a short distance east

neighborhoods.name: Stonestown
neighborhoods.intro: Stonestown surrounds the galleria and San Francisco State, and is largely apartments and newer development rather than detached houses. Very little single-family stock trades here.
near: The city's major west-side shopping center
The lake and loop trail to the west

neighborhoods.name: Lake Merced Park
neighborhoods.intro: Lake Merced Park is the parkland ringing the lake at the city's southwest corner. It appears in the neighborhood map as open space rather than a residential area.
near: A freshwater lake with a four-mile loop trail
The campus sits on the lake's eastern side

neighborhoods.name: Saint Francis Wood
neighborhoods.intro: Saint Francis Wood is the grandest of the city's planned residence parks — curving streets, formal fountains, mature trees and large houses on generous lots. It sits on the western slope of Mount Davidson, and its design covenants have kept the character intact.
near: Formal gates, fountains and curving streets
A village main street just north
The city's highest point, immediately east

neighborhoods.name: Forest Hill
neighborhoods.intro: Forest Hill winds up the hillside on streets laid out in the 1910s, with large homes on irregular lots and a private clubhouse at its center. The Muni station at its foot puts downtown within a short ride.
near: Muni Metro through the Twin Peaks Tunnel
Forested open space to the north

neighborhoods.name: Forest Hill Extension
neighborhoods.intro: Forest Hill Extension sits below and south of Forest Hill proper, on a more regular street pattern with somewhat smaller homes. It shares the same hillside setting and proximity to West Portal.
near: Muni Metro a short walk north

neighborhoods.name: West Portal
neighborhoods.intro: West Portal is the district's commercial heart, built around the avenue where four Muni Metro lines converge before entering the Twin Peaks Tunnel. The residential blocks around it are family-scaled and walkable, which is rare on this side of the city.
near: A village-scaled main street of independent shops
Four Muni Metro lines converge here

neighborhoods.name: Miraloma Park
neighborhoods.intro: Miraloma Park covers the slopes of Mount Davidson with mid-century homes on curving streets. It is quiet and consistently built, with the forested summit directly above.
near: The city's highest point, forested, directly above

neighborhoods.name: Monterey Heights
neighborhoods.intro: Monterey Heights occupies elevated blocks on the southwest side of Mount Davidson, with long southern views and generous lots. It is one of the quieter residence-park neighborhoods.

neighborhoods.name: Balboa Terrace
neighborhoods.intro: Balboa Terrace is a small, tightly covenanted residence park laid out in the same era as Saint Francis Wood, with consistent period homes on a compact street plan. Few properties trade in any given quarter.
near: Period covenants and consistent street frontage

neighborhoods.name: Westwood Park
neighborhoods.intro: Westwood Park is a bungalow neighborhood laid out on an oval street plan, unusually consistent in scale and period. It sits between Ocean Avenue and Monterey Boulevard.
near: A consistent bungalow tract from the 1910s

neighborhoods.name: Westwood Highlands
neighborhoods.intro: Westwood Highlands climbs the slope above Westwood Park, with larger homes and longer views. It is small, and only a handful of properties change hands each quarter.
near: Retail at the foot of the hill

neighborhoods.name: Sherwood Forest
neighborhoods.intro: Sherwood Forest occupies large lots high on the southern slope of Mount Davidson, one of the least dense pockets in the city. Turnover is very low.

neighborhoods.name: Mount Davidson Manor
neighborhoods.intro: Mount Davidson Manor sits at the district's western edge toward Ocean Avenue, with consistent detached homes on a regular grid. It is more attainable than the residence parks uphill.

neighborhoods.name: Ingleside Terraces
neighborhoods.intro: Ingleside Terraces is a residence park laid out on curving streets around a sundial, with larger homes than the Ingleside grid to the south. It is quiet and well-treed.
near: Curving streets around a central sundial

neighborhoods.name: Midtown Terrace
neighborhoods.intro: Midtown Terrace sits high on the eastern slope below Twin Peaks, a consistent tract of mid-century homes with wide views east across the city. Sutro Tower stands directly above it.
near: The summit and its views directly above
Forested open space to the north

neighborhoods.name: Diamond Heights
neighborhoods.intro: Diamond Heights occupies the ridge above Noe Valley and Glen Park, developed later than most of the city and so more varied in form — townhouses and mid-century homes alongside open space. The views run in several directions.
near: A wild canyon with trails at the southern edge
BART down the hill to the south

neighborhoods.name: Forest Knolls
neighborhoods.intro: Forest Knolls is a small mid-century tract on the wooded slope below Mount Sutro, reached by winding streets. Very few homes trade here in any quarter.
near: Muni Metro a short distance south
